prompt.context: Game Co. currently owns four casinos in Slot City. Competitors are contemplating opening up a rival casino in Libertyville. Game Co has hired Bain to assess the ramifications of a competitor opening a casino in Libertyville and Game Co.'s strategic options. Currently there are no casinos in Libertyville. There are competing casinos in Slot City but they are not relevant because it is a mature market. Slot City has a 25% tax on revenue. Libertyville has a 50% tax on revenues.
prompt.question: Question 1: What are the ramifications for existing revenue if a casino opens in Libertyville? Question 2: What are Game Co's options?

clarifying_info.q: What are Game Co.'s total revenues?
Where does Game Co.'s revenue come from geographically?
clarifying_info.a: Majority of revenues come from 4 cities: Slot City, Libertyville, Garden City, and Motor City (see exhibit). Garden City and Motor City are nearby, approximately 1 hour from Slot City. They are both approximately 2 hours from Libertyville. Libertyville is approximately 1 hour from Slot City. There are no casinos in Motor City or Garden City due to city regulations.

clarifying_info.q: How many customers does Game Co. have?
clarifying_info.a: Customer base is 1.8 million per year. All customers are evenly distributed across cities.

clarifying_info.q: Who are Game Co.'s customers / what are the customer segments?
clarifying_info.a: Three segments: Plug and Chuggers (hard core gamblers who only want to gamble and care most about convenience — assume casino payouts are identical across the board), Vacationers (want to 'get away' and leave the area for a week or weekend), and Experiencers (want to live the casino experience — lights, shows, action — and are interested in the casino itself and what it has to offer).

exhibits.title: Game Co. Revenue by City
exhibits.shows: Bar chart showing percentage of Game Co. total revenue attributable to each of four cities: Motor City, Slot City, Garden City, and Libertyville
exhibits.data: Y-axis: Percentage of revenue (0% to ~40%); X-axis categories: Motor City, Slot City, Garden City, Libertyville. Each bar shows approximate revenue share for that city. Libertyville appears to be the largest contributor (~35%), followed by Slot City (~30%), Garden City (~20%), Motor City (~15%).

framework: Revenues: Understand total revenues of Game Co. and where revenue comes from (type of services, geography)
Geographic location: Determine where Libertyville is relative to Slot City and the other feeder cities, and assess drive-time proximity
Customers: Identify customer segments, their preferences, and likelihood of switching to the new Libertyville competitor
Revenue at risk: Quantify which customer segments and geographies are exposed to defection
Strategic options: Evaluate Do Nothing vs. Open own casino in Libertyville (and sub-options to offset lost revenue)

questions.prompt: Which customer segments are at risk of switching to a new Libertyville casino, and by how much?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify the three segments and reason through each: Plug and Chuggers value convenience — a closer casino in Libertyville will draw them away 100%. Vacationers want to travel away from home — 0% will switch. Experiencers are attracted to the casino's offerings — some may switch; assume 50% for calculations. Candidate should also note that Motor City and Garden City customers are ~2 hr from Libertyville vs. ~1 hr from Slot City, so the additional drive time deters defection from those cities.

math.setup: Total revenues = $1.2B. Revenue is split across 4 cities. Libertyville customers represent approximately 35% of revenue (read from exhibit). Customers are evenly distributed across cities, so Libertyville = 25% of 1.8M = 450,000 customers. Segments are implicitly divided equally (candidate may assume even split or ask). Using equal thirds: ~150,000 Plug and Chuggers, ~150,000 Vacationers, ~150,000 Experiencers from Libertyville.
steps: Revenue at risk from Plug and Chuggers (Libertyville): 100% conversion × Libertyville P&C revenue share
Revenue at risk from Vacationers (Libertyville): 0% conversion = $0
Revenue at risk from Experiencers (Libertyville): 50% conversion × Libertyville Experiencer revenue share
Motor City and Garden City customers: additional drive time to Libertyville deters switching — treat as 0% conversion
Total revenue at risk ≈ Libertyville revenue × (1/3 × 100% + 1/3 × 0% + 1/3 × 50%) = Libertyville revenue × 50%
math.answer: If Libertyville revenue is ~35% of $1.2B ≈ $420M, revenue at risk ≈ $420M × 50% = ~$210M

questions.prompt: What are Game Co.'s strategic options in response to a competitor entering Libertyville?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify at least: (1) Do nothing — accept revenue loss; (2) Open own casino in Libertyville — cannibalize within the company rather than allow competitor to steal revenue. Key insight: it is more desirable to cannibalize within the company than to allow outside competitors to steal the revenue. Candidate should weigh tax rates (50% in Libertyville vs. 25% in Slot City) as a complication.

questions.prompt: Bonus: How can Game Co. make up for the lost revenues?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm revenue recovery levers across pricing, amenities, new streams, and demand stimulation.

brainstorming.prompt: How can Game Co. make up for the lost revenues if a competitor opens in Libertyville?

categories.name: Cost / Amenity reduction
ideas: Eliminate amenities such as free drinks

categories.name: Demand stimulation
ideas: Target customers in cities near Libertyville but far from Slot City
Steal share from existing casinos in Slot City through marketing and loyalty programs

recommendation: Game Co. should open its own casino in Libertyville to retain customers who would otherwise defect to the competitor
The new casino will primarily affect Libertyville-based customers; Motor City and Garden City customers are insulated by travel distance
Cannibalization within Game Co. is preferable to ceding revenue to an outside competitor
risks: Competitor opens first and captures first-mover advantage
High construction and operating costs for the new Libertyville casino
Libertyville's 50% tax rate (vs. 25% in Slot City) compresses margins on the new property
Internal cannibalization of Slot City revenues if Slot City customers also shift to Libertyville
next_steps: Conduct detailed financial modeling of Libertyville casino economics under the 50% tax regime
Assess construction timeline to determine feasibility of opening before the competitor
Develop customer retention programs (loyalty, promotions) to mitigate near-term revenue loss
Explore demand-stimulation strategies in Motor City and Garden City to offset any revenue shortfall
